messages.subject: Low coverage and using readBismarkCoverage
parts:
Hello, 

I'm reading in a promoter bed file that contains four genes but for some samples one gene is not read in and I think it is because there is low coverage in that region for a few of the samples. I know for read.bismark you can alter the mincov argument. I was wondering if there is a similar argument for readBismarkCoverage or if there is another method for lowering the minimum coverage. Below is my code, which runs through a data frame of tumour and normal pairs: 

for (i in 1:nrow(combined)){
file.list=list(combined[i, 1], combined[i, 2])
name.normal <- paste((strsplit(combined[i, 1], "_")[[1]][3]), "N", sep="_")
name.tumour <- paste((strsplit(combined[i, 2], "_")[[1]][3]), "T", sep="_")
meth.diff.prom <- paste(name.tumour, "promotermethdiff", sep="_")
myobj = readBismarkCoverage(file.list,sample.id=list(name.normal, name.tumour),
assembly="hg19",treatment=c(0,1))
all.promoters = read.bed("MMR_promoters.final.bed")
reads_in_allpromoters = regionCounts(myobj, all.promoters)
all.prom.meth=unite(reads_in_allpromoters,destrand=F)
myDiff.prom=calculateDiffMeth(all.prom.meth)
write.table(myDiff.prom, meth.diff.prom, quote=FALSE) 
}

The all.promoters shows all four rows but the actual all.prom.meth only shows 3.

Hi,
newer versions (> 0.9.6) has the methRead() function (old name "read" ) which can read the the Bismark coverage file with mincov argument. 

Best,
Altuna
